whoIsThisFor.heading: Who is the Marketing Cloud Engagement Developer exam for?

personas.label: Marketing Cloud developers
personas.description: You build Marketing Cloud solutions with AMPscript, SSJS, and CloudPages, and want to demonstrate those development skills.

personas.label: Email developers moving to Marketing Cloud
personas.description: You know HTML and CSS for email and want to show that you can add data-driven content in Marketing Cloud.

personas.label: Integration specialists
personas.description: You connect Marketing Cloud with other systems and want to validate your API and automation skills.

examDifficulty.heading: Is the Marketing Cloud Engagement Developer Exam Hard?
examDifficulty.summary: This is a technical exam. It covers AMPscript and SSJS code, REST and SOAP integrations, and custom Journey Builder activities. Practical coding experience helps with both interpreting snippets and choosing an implementation.
bullets: 60 scored questions in 105 minutes, plus up to five unscored questions that do not count.
63% to pass, which is 38 correct answers out of 60.
Expect code-reading questions where you determine what AMPscript or SSJS does, or spot a problem.
Know REST and SOAP patterns, OAuth authentication, and which API fits a task.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Before scheduling, build several AMPscript emails and CloudPages, create SSJS Script Activities in Automation Studio, and make test REST API requests.

examFormat.heading: Marketing Cloud Engagement Developer Exam Format Explained
examFormat.intro: The exam is proctored online or at a test center. It includes scenario questions about data retrieval, language choice, and integration design.
examFormat.scenarioPercent: About 50–60% of questions use scenarios. You may need to select an AMPscript function, choose between AMPscript and SSJS, or plan an API integration.
bestWayToPass: Practice AMPscript data functions such as Lookup, LookupRows, LookupOrderedRows, InsertData, and UpdateData. Match each function to the data operation it performs.
Use AMPscript for email personalization and learn where SSJS is a better fit for richer logic or API work in CloudPages and Script Activities.
Review the Marketing Cloud REST endpoint families for contacts, messaging, and data, along with OAuth 2.0 client-credentials authentication.
Build CloudPages that accept forms and display dynamic content; practice handling submitted data safely.

certificationCard.description: The exam covers AMPscript and SSJS development, CloudPages, REST and SOAP APIs, and custom Journey Builder activities. The exam is 60 scored questions in 105 minutes, with a 63% pass mark, weighted towards Programmatic Languages (35%) and API (22%).

keyConcepts.h2: Marketing Cloud Engagement Developer: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: AMPscript for data and content
blocks.body: Use Lookup to return a field value and LookupRows to return matching rows. Row and Field navigate a rowset, while FOR/NEXT iterates through it. IIF handles a short inline condition; IF/ELSEIF/ENDIF supports branching. TreatAsContentArea renders a named content area. HTTPGet and HTTPPost make HTTP requests, and DateAdd and DateParse support date work. Choose a function based on the data or personalization task.

blocks.heading: SSJS on the Marketing Cloud server
blocks.body: Server-Side JavaScript runs in Marketing Cloud contexts, not in the visitor’s browser. It can use JavaScript alongside platform features for HTTP requests, Data Extension work, and more involved processing. It is available in email, landing pages, and Automation Studio Script Activities. Know the roles of Platform.Load, HTTP.Post, Retrieve, and DataExtension.Add, and when AMPscript is simpler for email personalization.

blocks.heading: CloudPages and reusable content
blocks.body: CloudPages can host landing pages, microsites, and forms. A page can capture submitted fields into a Data Extension, including through Smart Capture. Personalized URLs can carry subscriber context for a prefilled experience. In Content Builder, dynamic content rules select different email content for different audiences. Shared content blocks let teams reuse personalization logic.

blocks.heading: REST and SOAP integration
blocks.body: Marketing Cloud REST endpoints cover work such as contacts, Data Extensions, and message sends. SOAP remains available for objects including Subscriber, List, and TriggeredSend. An integration obtains an OAuth 2.0 client-credentials access token and sends it as a Bearer token. Be able to select the API and endpoint that match the operation.

blocks.heading: Automation Studio scripts
blocks.body: A Script Activity runs SSJS as one step in an Automation Studio workflow. Teams use it for data handling, external requests, or checks that are awkward to express in SQL. Combine it with Query, Data Extract, and File Transfer activities as needed. Use try/catch and a suitable error log; account for activity run-time limits.

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the Salesforce Marketing Cloud Engagement Developer Exam
scenarioTips.intro: The exam checks whether you can build and maintain Marketing Cloud solutions with AMPscript, SSJS, APIs, and custom activities. Practice reading code and choosing a design for a concrete requirement.

blocks.heading: AMPscript Proficiency
blocks.body: Know how to retrieve and update Data Extension data, use conditions and date or string functions, and place AMPscript in email fields and content.

blocks.heading: Server-Side JavaScript (SSJS)
blocks.body: Review SSJS in CloudPages and Script Activities, including Platform.Load and the Core library patterns for working with rows. Distinguish server-side code from browser JavaScript.

blocks.heading: REST & SOAP API Usage
blocks.body: Study REST resources for contacts, messaging, and data, plus OAuth client-credentials authentication. Recognize SOAP use cases too.

blocks.heading: Query Activities & Data Extensions
blocks.body: Practice Automation Studio SQL, joins, and destination actions such as overwrite and append.

nextCertsAfter.intro: These credentials build on related Marketing Cloud and marketing automation skills.

sampleQuestions.question: Which AMPscript function reads a matching field value from a Data Extension for an email?
options: RaiseError, which stops processing for the subscriber being rendered
Lookup
SystemDateToLocalDate, which converts a stored date into local time
InsertData, which writes a new row into the target data extension instead
sampleQuestions.explanation: Lookup reads one field from the Data Extension row that matches the supplied search conditions.
whyWrong: RaiseError halts the send for that subscriber.
That function performs date conversion.
InsertData writes rather than reads.

sampleQuestions.question: When is SSJS a better choice than AMPscript in a Marketing Cloud solution?
options: It would be the only language able to read from a sendable data extension
It renders more quickly than AMPscript does during a large email send
It would be required whenever an email contains more than one content block
It handles loops, objects and API calls more comfortably
sampleQuestions.explanation: SSJS is useful when the solution needs richer data structures, loops, or Marketing Cloud platform calls.
whyWrong: AMPscript reads data extensions perfectly well.
AMPscript is generally the faster choice for inline personalization.
Content block count has nothing to do with the language.

sampleQuestions.question: A CloudPage stores submitted form data in a Data Extension. What is the key safety step?
options: Validating and encoding the submitted input
Confirming that the data extension has a retention policy configured on it
Ensuring the page is published to the correct content folder in the account
Checking that the page uses the same template as the rest of the site
sampleQuestions.explanation: Validate and encode public form input before using it; this reduces injection risk and protects data quality.
whyWrong: Retention matters for storage, not for accepting input safely.
Folder location is housekeeping rather than a safety concern.
Template consistency is a presentation detail.

sampleQuestions.question: What does a Triggered Send definition let an integration do?
options: A reusable configuration for sending one message on demand
A journey entry source that evaluates a data extension every hour
A report showing which subscribers received a particular email send
A schedule that causes an email to be sent at a fixed time each day
sampleQuestions.explanation: Triggered sends are set up once and then invoked, usually via the API, to send a single message to one subscriber immediately.
whyWrong: Entry source evaluation is a Journey Builder setting.
Send reporting is produced by tracking.
Scheduled sending is configured in Automation Studio.

sampleQuestions.question: What must an external client obtain before it can call the Marketing Cloud REST API?
options: A Data Extension marked as sendable and related to subscribers
An access token obtained from the auth endpoint
A CloudPage published with a public URL for the system to call
A triggered send definition created and published in the account
sampleQuestions.explanation: The client uses Installed Package credentials to request an access token from the authentication endpoint.
whyWrong: Sendable extensions matter for sends, not for authenticating.
CloudPages are a different integration surface.
Triggered sends are one thing you might call, not a prerequisite.

sampleQuestions.question: What information does an Installed Package provide for an API integration?
options: It schedules the automations that run overnight in the account
It defines the retention rules applied to each data extension
It holds the credentials and scope for API access
It stores the email templates shared between the business units
sampleQuestions.explanation: Installed packages carry the client credentials and the permission scopes that an integration is granted.
whyWrong: Scheduling is configured in Automation Studio.
Retention is set per data extension.
Templates live in Content Builder.

sampleQuestions.question: Which source can an Automation Studio SQL query use for send history?
options: Data views exposed within the account
A Data Extension that the developer creates and populates by hand
The tracking tab on each of the individual email jobs that were sent
The All Subscribers list filtered to the relevant date range
sampleQuestions.explanation: Query data views such as _Sent, _Open, and _Click to access send and engagement records.
whyWrong: Manual population would be unmaintainable and immediately stale.
Per-job tracking is a user interface view, not a queryable source.
All Subscribers holds status rather than send history.

sampleQuestions.question: Why should a query over Marketing Cloud data views usually limit its date range?
options: It could scan far more data than it needs to
Queries without a date filter are rejected by the platform automatically
The results will be written to the wrong target data extension instead
Data views only return rows from the current calendar month in any case
sampleQuestions.explanation: A date condition limits the rows scanned and helps prevent a large query from timing out.
whyWrong: The platform does not reject them outright.
The target is set in the activity regardless of the filter.
Data views hold a longer history than one month.

sampleQuestions.question: If AMPscript fails while rendering one subscriber’s email, what is the likely result?
options: The send is paused until a developer corrects the error in the content
The entire send is cancelled and no subscriber receives the email at all
The email is sent with the failing block silently omitted from the content
That subscriber's message fails while others continue
sampleQuestions.explanation: AMPscript is evaluated for each subscriber; an error can fail that subscriber’s message while the rest of the send continues.
whyWrong: Sends are not paused for developer intervention.
A single failure does not cancel the send.
The message fails rather than rendering partially.

sampleQuestions.question: How can a team reuse the same personalization logic across many emails?
options: A CloudPage that each of the emails links out to when it is opened
A shared content block containing the logic
The same code pasted into each of the twelve individual email templates
A separate triggered send definition created for each of the emails
sampleQuestions.explanation: Put the logic in one shared content block so every email can use the same maintained version.
whyWrong: Sending readers to a web page is not personalization of the email.
Twelve copies means twelve places to fix every bug.
Triggered sends are about sending, not sharing logic.

sampleQuestions.question: What makes a Data Extension sendable?
options: It would be permitted to hold more rows than a non-sendable extension can
It would be visible to every business unit configured within the account
It would be backed up automatically each night by the platform itself
It would be related to subscribers so it can be used as an audience
sampleQuestions.explanation: A sendable Data Extension has a configured relationship to subscriber data, allowing it to serve as a send audience.
whyWrong: Row capacity is not affected by the sendable flag.
Visibility is governed by business unit and folders.
Backups are not a function of being sendable.

sampleQuestions.question: Which Journey Builder entry method lets an outside system add one contact on demand?
options: A Data Extension entry source re-evaluated once every fifteen minutes
An automation that imports a file each time the external system changes
An API event entry source
A triggered send definition invoked directly by the external system
sampleQuestions.explanation: An API event can pass an individual contact into Journey Builder when the external system signals it.
whyWrong: A re-evaluated extension is still batch and introduces delay.
File-based import is slower and more fragile than an event.
A triggered send sends a message rather than entering a journey.

sampleQuestions.question: Why keep changeable settings in a Data Extension instead of hard-coding them?
options: The platform imposes a strict limit on the length of any AMPscript block
They can be changed without editing and republishing content
Data extensions are able to execute the logic that uses those values
Values held in a data extension are encrypted by the platform by default
sampleQuestions.explanation: Externalising values means a marketer or admin can change behaviour without a developer touching the content.
whyWrong: Block length is not the reason to externalise configuration.
Data extensions store data; they do not execute logic.
There is no automatic encryption of ordinary stored values.

sampleQuestions.question: How can one email show different content to subscribers in two countries?
options: Two separate emails, each one sent to its own country segment
A CloudPage that detects the recipient's location when they open it
Conditional content driven by a country attribute
Two triggered send definitions, one configured for each of the countries
sampleQuestions.explanation: Use conditional content based on the country attribute so one email can be maintained.
whyWrong: Two emails doubles the maintenance for the same outcome.
Detecting location on open is unreliable and happens too late.
Triggered sends do not solve a content variation problem.

sampleQuestions.question: What work does a Marketing Cloud developer primarily deliver?
options: Deciding which audiences each of the marketing campaigns should target
Designing the visual layout and copy used in each of the email templates
Building the data, logic and integrations behind the campaigns
Managing the account's sending reputation and deliverability over time
sampleQuestions.explanation: The developer builds the plumbing: data models, queries, personalisation logic, cloud pages and API integrations that campaigns run on.
whyWrong: Audience strategy is a marketing decision.
Visual design and copy sit with the marketing team.
Deliverability is usually an operational or consulting responsibility.
